Wind prone areas along US-395/I-580 may see gusts up to 65 mph. * WHERE...In California, Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra Counties. In Nevada, Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area. * WHEN...From 10 AM to 10 PM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds may knock down burned trees in the Davis Fire, Hawk Fire, and Bull Fire burn areas.

location.region: Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra Counties; Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area

weather.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 12 at 11:56AM PST until November 13 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Reno NV
weather.description:
* CHANGES...None.

* WHAT...South to southwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 55
mph. Wind prone areas along US-395/I-580 may see gusts up to 65
mph.

* WHERE...In California, Lassen-Eastern Plumas-Eastern Sierra
Counties. In Nevada, Greater Reno-Carson City-Minden Area.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 10 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds may knock down burned trees in the Davis
Fire, Hawk Fire, and Bull Fire burn areas.
weather.instruction:
Now is the time to secure loose outdoor items such as patio
furniture, holiday decorations, and trash cans before winds increase
which could blow these items away. The best thing to do is prepare
ahead of time by making sure you have extra food and water on hand,
flashlights with spare batteries and/or candles in the event of a
power outage.

the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be: 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:10 PM Thursday 11/12, 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through Monday.

will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.

capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to 2
inches. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph through Friday, then 60 mph
Saturday into Sunday.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...We are expecting a lull in snowfall beginning
Friday afternoon through Saturday evening before snowfall chances
increase Saturday night into Sunday morning. With the lull in snow
and winds, expect higher visibilities. Winds will increase
thereafter and be strongest on Saturday afternoon into Sunday with
gusts as high as 60 mph possible, with blizzard conditions
returning.
weather.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. If you must travel,
have a winter survival kit with you. If you get stranded, stay with
your vehicle.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. * WHERE...Tillamook County Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon to 4 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from noon Friday to noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level, during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition, the Garibaldi tidal gauge is forecast to reach approximately 10.5 ft during high tide Friday afternoon. This typically results in flooding over Burton-Fraser Rd. along the Tillamook River.

location.region: Tillamook County Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 10:22AM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding
expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous
surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Tillamook County Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon to 4 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from noon Friday to noon
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Garibaldi tidal gauge is forecast to reach approximately
10.5 ft during high tide Friday afternoon. This typically
results in flooding over Burton-Fraser Rd. along the Tillamook
River.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. * WHERE...Clatsop County Coast and Central Coast of Oregon. * WHEN...From noon Friday to noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 10:22AM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to
30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Clatsop County Coast and Central Coast of Oregon.

* WHEN...From noon Friday to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock
people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid
ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The
sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.
weather.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.25 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast. * WHERE...Grays Harbor County Coast zone. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 5 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Friday to 7 AM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures expected. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate coastal erosion.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.25 feet above ground level
is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas. For
the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Grays Harbor County Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 5 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Friday to 7 AM
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected. Large breaking waves can knock people off
their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks
and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing
the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

closures.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through Monday.

For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

events.description: * WHAT...Snow and mixed precipitation. events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.25 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast. * WHERE...Grays Harbor County Coast zone. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 5 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Friday to 7 AM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures expected. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate coastal erosion.

location.region: Grays Harbor County Coast

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 4:31AM PST until November 13 at 5:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. Inundation of 1.75 to 2.25 feet above ground level
is possible along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas. For
the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Grays Harbor County Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 5 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Friday to 7 AM
PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected. Large breaking waves can knock people off
their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks
and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing
the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Brookings. * WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 10 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. events.description: * WHAT...For the Storm Warning, south winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts up to 55 kt and very steep seas 15 to 19 ft at 10 to 14 seconds. For the Gale Warning, from 9 AM this morning to 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 4 PM this afternoon to 1 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced. Bar crossings will be especially dangerous. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Another strong front will move in late Saturday and Saturday night with the potential for storm force winds and very steep and hazardous seas. This front will be followed by another round of very high westerly swell Sunday into Monday. Please continue to monitor the forecast for updates on this high impact weather pattern. * View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. * WHERE...Clatsop County Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon today to 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from noon today to noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level, during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak this evening and tonight. In addition, the Astoria Tide gauge is forecast to reach approximately 10.6 ft during high tide this afternoon.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding

surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Clatsop County Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon today to 4 PM
PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from noon today
to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak this evening and tonight. In addition, the
Astoria Tide gauge is forecast to reach approximately 10.6 ft
during high tide this afternoon.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night. Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at elevations of 2,500 feet, mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160 near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on Friday night.

events.title: Coastal Flood Statement
events.description: * WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways (3.2 to 11.6 feet Mean Lower Low Water). * WHERE...Barnstable MA and Nantucket MA Counties. * WHEN...Friday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Roads remain passable. Low lying areas and roads near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy Street, may experience pockets of shallow flooding less than one foot deep. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Splashover and very minor coastal flooding are possible during the Friday afternoon high tide along north facing beaches on Cape Cod Bay as well as Nantucket sound. No significant impacts are expected and any splashover/very minor coastal flooding will be quite short- lived, no more than an hour on either side of high tide.

location.region: Barnstable; Nantucket

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night. Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at elevations above 2,500 feet with mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160 near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on Friday night.

events.title: Blizzard Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph through Friday, then 60 mph Saturday into Sunday. * WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast. * WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard conditions will be intermittently possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...We are expecting a lull in snowfall beginning Friday afternoon through Saturday evening before snowfall chances increase Saturday night into Sunday morning. With the lull in snow and winds, expect higher visibilities. Winds will increase thereafter and be strongest on Saturday afternoon into Sunday with gusts as high as 60 mph possible, with blizzard conditions returning.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph through Friday, then 60 mph
Saturday into Sunday.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...We are expecting a lull in snowfall beginning
Friday afternoon through Saturday evening before snowfall chances
increase Saturday night into Sunday morning. With the lull in snow
and winds, expect higher visibilities. Winds will increase
thereafter and be strongest on Saturday afternoon into Sunday with
gusts as high as 60 mph possible, with blizzard conditions
returning.
weather.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. A Blizzard Warning
means severe winter weather conditions are expected or occurring.
Falling and blowing snow with strong winds are likely. This could
lead to whiteout conditions, making travel extremely dangerous. If
you must travel, have a winter survival kit with you. If you get
stranded, stay in your vehicle.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Wednesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill. Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 AM CST Friday the stage was 10.0 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early Sunday afternoon to a crest of 15.0 feet Monday morning. It will then fall below flood stage late Tuesday evening. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2 feet on 09/19/1983. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: McMullen, TX

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:17AM CST until November 18 at 2:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon to Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CST Friday the stage was 10.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Sunday afternoon to a crest of 15.0 feet Monday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage late Tuesday evening.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 09/19/1983.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey Bay. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM today to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

events.description: * WHAT...Snow and mixed precipitation. Total snow accumulations from 2 to 10 inches. * WHERE...Kodiak Island Northeast. * WHEN...Until 11 PM AKST this evening. * IMPACTS...Heavy snow and rain on snow may create difficult travel conditions. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A compact storm will move southeast of Kodiak Island and remain nearly stationary through Friday afternoon to evening. Slight deviations in the storm position to the east and west will cause snow levels to fluctuate between sea level and 400 ft in elevation. events.title: Winter Storm Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Moderate to heavy snowfall possible. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), East Turnagain Arm, Western Kenai Peninsula, Southern Kenai Mtns, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through late Sunday night. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Longwave troughing in the Bering Sea hedges east as inverted troughing in the Gulf of Alaska tracks west. A snow band will set up and stall over Anchorage/Kenai Peninsula tomorrow afternoon through Sunday bringing rounds of moderate to heavy snowfall. There is moderate uncertainty as to where the snow band will ultimately end up, resulting in lower confidence for snowfall amounts. Warmer temperatures filters in Sunday afternoon from east to west, transitioning snow to rain. *Low/High end values are as follows: - Anchorage/Eagle River & western Kenai Peninsula: 2-4" (Low end)/6-10" (High end). Higher elevations: up to a foot possible. - Seward: 1-3" (Low end)/3-6" (High end). - Turnagain Pass to Moose Pass: 7 to 11" possible. - Portage: 9-11" with snowfall rates of up to 1" an hour.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. * WHERE...South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level, during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition, the Toke Point tidal gage is forecast to reach 11.2 feet during high tide Friday afternoon, which is high enough to result in tidal overflow flooding for a few hours around high tide.

weather.description:

conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected.

* WHERE...South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Toke Point tidal gage is forecast to reach 11.2 feet during
high tide Friday afternoon, which is high enough to result in
tidal overflow flooding for a few hours around high tide.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in port, or take
shelter until winds and waves subside. Commercial vessels should

and waves subside.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, moderate to significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west- northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST this evening. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM this evening to 3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain far away from the water's edge. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. events.description: * WHAT...Snow is expected for elevations above 6000 feet. Total snow accumulations 6 to 12 inches, with up to 18 inches at the highest peaks. Minor accumulations of around an 2 inch possible down to 5000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 60 mph. * WHERE...Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50, Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108, Southern Cascades above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park. * WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Friday evening commute. Strong winds could cause downed tree branches, localized power outages, and reduced visibilities. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 6500 to 7500 feet Today, dropping to 5500 to 6000 feet Saturday morning. Heaviest snowfall expected this afternoon through the overnight hours. Snowfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour, with locally up to 3 inches per hour in convective bands. Light flurries to 2 inches possible down to 5000 feet with higher accumulations remaining above 6000 feet. Lull in activity Saturday afternoon through Sunday, followed by additional snow Sunday night through Monday.

events.title: Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected. * WHERE...Extreme Southeast Central Cook County in northeastern Illinois... Central Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana... * WHEN...Until 900 AM CST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and ditches may be clogged with debris, increasing the risk of flooding. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 153 PM CST, Doppler radar indicated lake effect rain. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain has fallen since Thursday evening. Several creeks and streams are rising, including the Turkey Creek near Merrillville which has recently risen above bankfull. - Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... The Far East side of Chicago, Hammond, Gary, Calumet City, Merrillville, South Shore, East Chicago, Schererville, Hobart, Lansing, Crown Point, Highland, Munster, Cedar Lake, Griffith, Dyer, South Deering, St. John, Lake Station, Lynwood, Lakes of the Four Seasons, Whiting, Winfield and New Chicago. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
